22.0.0.en: In any case: without doubt or hesitation.

22.0.1.en: The Law highlights the importance of mercy in returning a stray ox or sheep to its owner if he is one of the Jews. The Book of Exodus (Ex 23:4) mentions returning a stray animal to an enemy; and in the New Testament, in the parable of the Good Samaritan, Christ showed that the neighbor is every human being (Lk 10:30-36).

22.1.0.en: If you do not know the owner of the stray animal, keep it in your house until its owner seeks it, and then you give it to him.

22.2.0.en: In any similar circumstance in which a neighbor or relative loses some of his possessions, such as one of his animals or his garment or anything else, you must do what you can to return the lost thing to its owner, and not neglect it.

22.3.0.en: The Law requires helping any Jew whose ox or donkey has fallen under its load, so that he can continue on his way. The Book of Exodus also commanded helping an enemy if his ox or donkey has fallen under its load (Ex 23:5).

22.4.0.en: God desires by this commandment that each person behave according to the nature with which God created him. If a woman puts on a man's clothes, she may forget her gentleness and behave roughly like a man; likewise, a man who puts on a woman's clothes may incline toward effeminacy. So both man and woman must observe modesty in their dress and not depart from custom and moderation, and this also resists the habit of sexual perversion.

22.5.0.en: If you happen upon a bird's nest on the way, in a tree or on the ground, with the mother sitting on her eggs or her young, it is not lawful for you to take both the mother and the young, but you must take only the young for yourself and let the mother go.

22.5.1.en: This legislation shows the extent of the Lord's care for all His creation, even the birds, and it also shows the importance of the mother and the appreciation of her role in preserving the species, for it is the mother who brings forth the eggs and not the reverse.

22.5.2.en: The reward announced for carrying out this commandment reminds us of the fifth commandment, which orders the honoring of parents in (Ex 20:12), "that thy days may be long upon the land." While the Jews considered the commandment concerning birds to be the least of the commandments in the Law, the Lord affirms the high standing of motherhood in the world of animals and birds as in the world of men, that is, His sanctification of motherhood in all its forms.

22.6.0.en: The roofs of houses in the East are flat, and they were used for many purposes, among them sitting in the winter sun and sleeping in the summer to enjoy the pleasant air; guests were also received on them, and they were used for storing some things, and so on. So Moses commands the owner of the house to build a parapet for the roof, so that no one falls from it by accident and the owner of the house be held responsible for the blood of the one who fell. The wisdom of this commandment is that a person must not expose his brother to harm, but must take everything necessary to preserve the lives of others, for the Lord cares for the lives and safety of people.

22.6.1.en: The spirit of love and compassion for others will extend spontaneously to compassion for animals and plants. So be merciful to all, that you may obtain God's mercies. Put yourself in the place of everyone before you deal with him, so that you may feel with him, make excuses for him, and be tender toward him.

22.7.0.en: The fullness ("seed"): everything that has been sown.

22.7.1.en: What is meant here is not sowing two different kinds of grain at one time in the same field. Naturally, each kind has its own system, different from the other, in irrigation and care, so that it may grow and be harvested at its own time, which may differ from the other's.

22.7.2.en: Lest the fullness be defiled ("sanctified"): meaning that everything that has been sown is subject to the application of the law of the firstfruits and the tithes for each kind separately, that is, he offers the firstfruits of each kind and the tithes of each kind, which may confuse the owner of the field and expose him to error and shortcoming in the Lord's rights. This is also a symbol of undesirable mixing with the wicked. This law was mentioned in (Lev 19:19).

22.8.0.en: You shall not yoke an ox and a donkey together under one yoke, because the ox is stronger than the donkey, and therefore the donkey cannot keep up with the ox in the length of its stride and its endurance, so the donkey is exhausted. It is well known that the ox is among the clean animals in the Law, while the donkey is among the unclean.

22.8.1.en: In this is a warning to the believer not to assign two people who differ in ability and gifts to do the same work, but to ask of each one what suits his mental, physical, and health capacities. Likewise, spiritually, believers are not to mix with unbelievers, in application of the Apostle's saying in (2 Cor 6:14), lest they become like them and share with them in their evil works.

22.9.0.en: Wool and linen each have natural properties that differ from one another, so the life of a garment woven from a mixture of the two is determined by the life of the kind that wears out faster, which causes the loss of the whole garment. Spiritually, the people of God must be distinguished by purity and be one fabric, with one spirit and one mind.

22.9.1.en: We note here that verses (9-11) are all symbolic images urging us not to mix contradictory things, and calling us to acquire the spirit of discernment between divine truth and the falsehood of the world, between purity and uncleanness, between holiness and license, between uprightness and deviation.

22.9.2.en: Be careful that concern for God and for the world do not mix in your heart, but let your whole heart be God's, and then use the world as a gift from God and do not cling to it for its own sake.

22.10.0.en: Tassels: threads that hang from the corners of the garment.

22.10.1.en: The purpose of this commandment is to distinguish the outward appearance of the Lord's people from the other peoples, so that the believer may be distinguished in his conduct and behavior from the people of the world, because clothes symbolize conduct.

22.11.0.en: If a man marries a young woman and, after having relations with her, hates her and accuses her of not having been a virgin before the marriage, whether this is a true accusation, that is, he did not find in her the sign proving that she was a virgin, or his accusation was false and he claimed it because of his hatred of her.

22.12.0.en: The young woman's parents bring the case before the elders of the city, who undertake the judging in the court, whose seat is at the gate of the city (as a place known to everyone), and they present to them the sign of their daughter's virginity that appeared on the day of her marriage, since the family of the bride in the East, and in some places even now, took care to keep this sign to prove her virginity before marriage; but with the progress of civilization this custom has faded, out of consideration for the bride's feelings and her modesty.

22.13.0.en: The parents declare before the judges that the husband hated their daughter and that this is the reason he spread his false rumor that she was not a virgin, and here is the sign of virginity presented before them, which is their daughter's garment bearing the sign of her virginity.

22.14.0.en: The judges, on the basis of the evidence presented which proves the innocence of the young woman, rule that the husband be disciplined in some way (beating, rebuke, or otherwise)... and as compensation to the young woman whose innocence has been proved and whose reputation has been restored, they rule that the husband be fined one hundred shekels of silver, which he pays to the young woman's father. This is considered a ruling that the family's reputation is sound, and this fine is double the dowry that is paid at marriage (v. 28).

22.15.0.en: Here the commandment addresses another case, which is that the charge is proved against the young woman and the husband was truthful in his claim against her.

22.16.0.en: The judges bring her to the door of her father's house, as an indication of that house's failure in raising the daughter and the father's negligence in watching over her conduct, which caused the young woman's deviation and her committing a vile transgression unbecoming to the daughters of the holy people while she was still in her father's house, and she is stoned there to death. By this sentence, by which they are rid of this young woman, they will have put away evil from their midst.

22.17.0.en: Adultery with a married woman is a crime in the Jewish Law, and its penalty is the stoning to death of the man and the woman: the man is stoned here because he violated his brother's honor, and the woman because she betrayed her husband (Lev 20:10).

22.18.0.en: In the case of a man committing adultery with a betrothed young woman, who is considered in the position of a married woman, as the Virgin and Joseph the carpenter were (Mt 1:20,) and this adultery takes place inside a populated city, both are sentenced to stoning: the man because he violated his brother's honor, and the young woman because she did not cry out for help to the people, which means that she consented to this adultery.

22.19.0.en: In the case of a man committing adultery with a betrothed young woman in the field, that is, in a place far from people, if the young woman cries out no one will hear her, so they stone the man, but for the young woman they find an excuse, because the man took advantage of her physical weakness, just as a man falls upon his brother in the field and kills him and he has no chance to call on anyone for help.

22.20.0.en: In the case of the discovery that a man has assaulted a virgin young woman who is not betrothed, the Law rules in this case that the man pay her father fifty (shekels) of silver (which is the same sum paid as a dowry for a wife). He must marry her because he assaulted her, and he cannot divorce her afterward all his life. But if her father refuses his marrying his daughter, he does not marry her; this is the young woman's right, but there is no compulsion on her to marry the one who assaulted her (Ex 22:16, 17).

22.21.0.en: His father's skirt: the skirt is the edge of the garment, and his father's skirt means that he lifted the garments of his father's wife and assaulted her in adultery.

22.21.1.en: It is not permissible for a son to marry his father's wife in any circumstances, whether during his father's lifetime if he has divorced her, or after his death when she has become a widow.

22.21.2.en: So when Reuben committed adultery with his father Jacob's wife, he was deprived of the birthright (Gen 48:22), and when Absalom assaulted the concubines of his father David, he died a shameful death in the war (2 Sam 16:22, 18:14, 15), and as a son in Corinth assaulted his father's wife, St. Paul the Apostle put him out of the Church for a time (1 Cor 5:

22.21.4.en: Be chaste in refusing any evil look, and reject every wicked thought, so that you may live in purity with everyone, and God will bless you and everyone will be at ease with you.

22.21.5.en: The purity of the people, vows, and the freedom and property of others

23.0.s.en: (1) The admission of peoples into the assembly of the Lord

23.0.0.en: One emasculated by crushing: one who is castrated by crushing his testicles with a piece of stone or the like.

23.0.1.en: One mutilated: one who is castrated by cutting off the testicles with a sharp instrument.

23.0.2.en: The assembly of the Lord: the people of Israel, who entered into a covenant with the Lord that binds them to specific regulations, acts of worship, and rituals.

23.0.3.en: The purpose of this commandment is to prevent the castration of some persons for the purpose of dedicating them to service, as the pagans used to do, whether in their pagan temples or in the palaces of their kings, especially for serving the women, thinking that this is a kind of worship that pleases their gods. The Law excluded the eunuch from membership in the assembly of the Lord. For the Lord wanted His people not to imitate the pagans in their perverse deeds, and He also wanted to affirm to His people the sanctity of all the members of the body and to change the view of the sexual organs as defiled members.

23.0.4.en: And exclusion from membership means exclusion from enjoying full rights; they are not prevented from worshipping the Lord, but such a person is barred from practicing certain spiritual or leadership functions, such as the priesthood or being one of the leaders of the people.

23.1.0.en: Even to the tenth generation: this is a long time, meaning throughout the generations, and in another expression, not even after the tenth generation.

23.1.1.en: The son born as a result of an adulterous relationship is considered excluded from entering the assembly of the Lord. They are deprived of some rights, but this does not prevent any of them from worshipping God and having a place in eternal life, because he is not at fault.

23.1.2.en: The Lord established this for the following reasons:

23.1.3.en: 1- So that the people would hate the sin of adultery, which is an uncleanness.

23.1.4.en: 2- This son might also regard adultery as permissible and so spread this sin.

23.1.5.en: Some of them did attain a position of leadership, such as Jephthah the Gileadite (Judg 11:1-29).

23.2.0.en: Ammonite or Moabite: they are the descendants of Lot (Gen 19:37, 38). The Lord forbade any Ammonite or Moabite to enter the assembly of the Lord. The reason for the prohibition is what they did toward their cousins, the children of Israel, in the story of the Exodus from Egypt. For they did not supply them with their need of bread and water, whether by honoring them as guests and cousins, nor did they even agree to sell to them for a price. In addition, they summoned Balaam the son of Beor to curse them (Num 22, 23, 24). Nehemiah carried this out by excluding Tobiah the Ammonite and not dealing with him (Neh 13:7, 8). This means that the Moabites and the Ammonites were marked by two evil traits:

23.2.1.en: 1- Harshness in their treatment of the children of Israel.

23.2.2.en: 2- Hatred and revenge, as appeared in the matter of Balaam.

23.2.3.en: So the purpose of excluding them was their insistence on harming the children of Israel, but whoever believes in God and wants to join His people is accepted, like Ruth the Moabitess, who not only joined the people of God but became a grandmother of Christ.

23.3.0.en: The attempts of the Moabites to curse the holy people through Balaam did not succeed, because the Lord turned the curse into a blessing out of love for His people whom He had acquired for Himself.

23.4.0.en: God forbade them to make a peace treaty with them or to try to benefit from their good things, but to keep away from them all their lives because they persist in evil, so that they would not be defiled by the worship of their idols.

23.5.0.en: The Edomites are the descendants of Esau, the brother of Jacob, so they and the children of Israel are brothers; therefore the Lord commands them not to hate them.

23.5.1.en: Likewise the Egyptians, for they dwelt for a time in their land and enjoyed their good things, and they received them as guests and overwhelmed them with their generosity and kindness in the days of Joseph; therefore those of them who live as resident aliens in Israel may be accepted into the assembly of the Lord in the third generation only, and are not rejected forever as is the case with the Ammonites and Moabites, that is, the Edomite himself is not accepted, but the third generation of the Edomite married to the Jews, and the third generation means the children of the grandchildren. This makes clear that God keeps them away from certain peoples because of their abundant evil, such as Moab and the children of Ammon, but they love the Gentiles, with caution against the worship of idols and evil lusts; therefore they admit the third generation, which has been purified by the knowledge of God, so that it can worship Him and become a member of the assembly of God. And even the wicked, such as the Moabites, they do not treat as enemies but only separate themselves from them (ch. 2:9, 19).

23.5.2.en: Have love toward all the people around you, however wrongdoing and wicked they may be, but beware of excessive mixing with them, lest you be defiled by their strange thoughts and evil ways, and be careful, you and your sons and your grandsons, but teach your children to love everyone and to pray for everyone.

23.6.1.en: He commands them that the warriors be committed to purity and keep away from everything unclean.

23.7.0.en: What chances by night: a nocturnal emission, that is, the discharge of seminal fluid.

23.7.1.en: The camp: the encampment, that is, the place where the warriors stay.

23.7.2.en: If one of the men has a nocturnal emission while sleeping, in the morning he goes outside the camp and stays there until evening, then he washes and is purified and enters the camp.

23.8.0.en: The second thing that the children of Israel observe is going outside the camp in order to dispose of their waste, so they designate a place for this, and the man goes out with a peg and digs a hole to relieve himself, then covers the excrement with earth.

23.9.0.en: The Lord explains the reason for the commandment concerning the two previous matters, which is the presence of God in the midst of His host, in order to fight for them and defeat their enemies. Therefore the camp must be pure and holy, lest God see in it something filthy that defiles the state of purity, and He leave them and not be in their midst.

23.9.1.en: And the observance of outward cleanliness points to inward purity and encourages its observance, for it constantly reminds them that they are a holy people, pure spiritually as they are bodily.

23.9.2.en: May you prepare for the Divine Liturgy with repentance, prayers, and purity of body, because you will meet God and be united with Him.

23.10.0.en: Escaped to you: has fled to you.

23.10.1.en: In one of your gates: in one of your cities.

23.10.2.en: The servant who suffered from the mistreatment of his master, whether from the people of Israel or from other peoples, and fled from him and took refuge with you seeking protection, it is not right for you to return him to his master, but you allow him to dwell among you in the place he chooses and in the city where he asks to stay, and you shall not oppress him, but treat him well as one of you, even if this servant is a pagan or from an enemy people.

23.10.3.en: This law protects the servant from exploitation, torture, and killing if his master catches him, as was customary among the ancient peoples.

23.10.4.en: And it is not understood from this commandment that a runaway servant is to be helped if he has committed a crime, but in this case he should be tried and held accountable.

23.10.5.en: Nor is it understood that the runaway servant is to be exploited to be a servant among the Jews, but they accept him as one wronged and give him a place to live as a human being, because the Law states that everything lost is to be returned to its owner (Ex 23:4). And by this commandment God implicitly resists the slavery that prevailed at that time, and so helps to free the wronged servant.

23.10.6.en: Be merciful and hasten to the aid of everyone who cries out to you, and help him and have compassion on him even if he wronged you before, for this is your opportunity to show him the love of Christ.

23.11.0.en: Sodomite: effeminate, sexually perverse, that is, one with whom a male has relations, treating him as in the place of a female.

23.11.2.en: God forbids His people adultery and sexual perversion, and God does not accept a vow offered to Him in His house that comes from the wages of adultery or sexual perversion.

23.11.3.en: Be careful and keep away from evil sights, wicked company, and all places that cause you to stumble, so that you may be His son and worship Him in purity.

23.12.0.en: The Lord forbids the members of His people to lend to one another by taking interest (usury) on these loans, whether lending money, food, or anything else. As for lending to pagan foreigners, they may lend to them while collecting interest on those loans (Ex 22:25). For the members of the people among themselves, they had to live in a spirit of fellowship, because all that they have is a divine gift to them all, for they are one family, in addition to the fact that the one who borrows faces difficult circumstances, so it is not right to exploit the need of the brethren to make a profit. As for foreigners, collecting interest on loans was a practice in force among them and followed in their laws, so this is not new to them. But for the people of God it is a special privilege of theirs, which makes them feel sympathy, spiritual brotherhood, and mutual support among themselves.

23.12.1.en: Have compassion on those in financial distress, lend to them and do not take interest; indeed, may you not demand repayment of their debts either, and consider that part of your tithes and gifts, because it is God who blessed you and gave you everything you have, so do not be harsh on debtors. But if your heart doubts the need of the one who asks of you, give only a little, so that you will not be troubled if he does not repay you.

23.13.0.en: A person who makes a vow to the Lord must not delay fulfilling it, because the Lord is required to carry it out, so any delay or refusal to fulfill the vow is counted by the Lord as sin against him. Therefore haste in uttering a vow is not advisable, but the matter is taken with all seriousness.

23.14.0.en: The Lord obliges no one to vow. Individuals have complete freedom to vow or not to vow. If someone vows, let him do so with all love and all determination to fulfill it, not out of compulsion but with love and gratitude. And if he refrains from vowing at the outset, there is no sin on him, for the Lord does not need vows.

23.15.0.en: Everything a person promises in his vow, he becomes bound to fulfill exactly as he promised, that is, in the same measure and form in which he vowed. The offering is a voluntary offering that no one forced him to make.

23.15.1.en: God rejoices in your gifts because they are proof of your love, and He answers your requests because you are His child; but if you are unable to make a vow, do not rush and promise God it, and if you vow, write it down with you so that you do not forget it and may be faithful to God.

23.16.0.en: This verse and the one that follows are educational teaching about the vineyard and meeting the need of the hungry. The Law permits the passerby to enter another's vineyard to satisfy his hunger, and he may eat enough to satisfy his hunger, but he must not be greedy and carry some away with him as he leaves, taking advantage of the generosity of its owner.

23.17.0.en: Sickle: a curved iron tool with a wooden handle with which the farmer cuts the stalks of wheat after it ripens.

23.17.1.en: The same applies if a person enters a field owned by another, he may pluck the ears with his hands to eat as much as he needs, but he does not use a sickle to reap with, for the harvest is the right of the owner of the field, and he awaits its time to rejoice in it. The disciples of Christ did this when they were hungry and ate from the ears of the field (Mt 12:1-8).

23.17.2.en: Do not look with an eye of envy or jealousy at the possessions of others and covet them, especially if he treats you well, but be content with what you have and thank God, and if someone gives you something, thank him, so as to return love for love. And in proportion to your awareness of God's gifts to you, you will become contented, satisfied, and kind to everyone.

23.17.3.en: Divorce, marriage, justice, and compassion for the needy
